short: The first emperor, whose forty-year settlement replaced the Republic with rule dressed as restoration.
full:
On 16 January 27 BCE the Senate granted Octavian, victor over Antony and Cleopatra at Actium, the honorific Augustus. He kept the old republican offices and titles but concentrated their powers in one man, calling himself princeps, first citizen, rather than king or dictator. Behind that fiction lay standing control of the army, the treasury, and the provinces where the legions were stationed.

Augustus's forty-one years brought peace after a century of civil war, a professional standing army, a reorganised tax system, and a building programme that remade Rome in marble. He never resolved succession cleanly, outliving chosen heirs before settling on his stepson Tiberius. He died on 19 August 14 CE, and the Senate declared him a god. The system he built, workable only because no one could openly call it monarchy, endured for centuries.
